name: Parallel Bar Support Hold
summary: An isometric calisthenics exercise where the body is supported on parallel bars with locked elbows and active shoulder depression.

setup: Mount the parallel bars or dip station by placing a hand on each bar using a neutral grip.
Jump or press yourself up until your arms are fully extended and your feet are clear of the floor or footrests.
steps: Depress your shoulders forcefully downward, actively pushing the bars away to create maximum distance between your ears and shoulders.
Maintain straight, locked-out elbows without hyper-extending.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes, keeping your legs straight or slightly crossed underneath you in a stable hollow-body posture.
Hold this rigid position for the target duration before safely stepping or lowering down.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and continuously into the diaphragm while maintaining constant abdominal and shoulder tension.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward toward the ears (passive hang).
common_faults.correction: Actively press down through the hands to engage the lower traps and depress the scapulae.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the elbows to bend under fatigue.
common_faults.correction: Keep the elbows fully extended and contract the triceps throughout the hold.
Engage the abdominals and squeeze the glutes to keep the pelvis neutral.

precautions: Ensure the bars are securely anchored and spaced appropriately to shoulder width.
Terminate the hold before losing scapular depression to protect the shoulders from excessive passive stress.
